title: Personal finance
audience: a high-school student (grades 9–12) or an adult reviewing high-school work
purpose: Plan income and spending, use bank accounts and payment tools wisely, understand taxes and how to file, use credit and loans responsibly, compare student-loan and college-cost options, protect yourself with insurance, and start investing and retirement saving with an understanding of risk, return, diversification and fees.

weeks.1: Earning income: jobs, paychecks and benefits
weeks.4: Taxes: how income tax works and filing a simple return
weeks.5: Credit reports, credit scores and credit cards
weeks.6: Loans: car loans, student loans and amortization
weeks.7: Paying for college: aid, scholarships and loans
weeks.9: Insurance: health, auto, renters and life
weeks.10: Investing basics: stocks, bonds, funds, risk and return
weeks.12: Consumer protection, fraud and financial decisions

blocks.deliverable: Build a monthly budget from a job offer.
Estimate the federal income tax on a simple return.
Compare two car loans by total interest paid.
Week 7 midterm; compare the total cost of two college plans.
Compare two funds by fees and diversification.
Project a retirement balance from age 22 to 67.
Submit the project; take an unseen 60 minute final in week 14.

project: Life plan: for a chosen first job, build a one-year budget with taxes and benefits, an emergency fund, a debt-repayment plan for a student loan, an insurance checklist, and a retirement savings plan with projected balances; present the plan and the three most important trade-offs.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
